blocks.text:
By email

Megan Sutton
Director of Operations
{{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}
Re: Crisis communications counsel
Dear Ms. Sutton:

Thank you for the confidence you and your colleagues have shown in us at a difficult moment for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} (the “Company”). This letter sets out the terms on which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC (the “Firm,” “we” or “us”) will provide crisis communications counsel to the Company. It replaces any earlier understanding about this work, whether written or oral.
The Matter and Our Role

The Company has asked us to advise on its communications concerning the recent operational disruption and its consequences for customers, employees, investors and the communities in which it operates (the “Matter”). Our role is advisory. We will recommend, draft and coordinate, and the Company will retain final authority over every statement made in its name.

In the opening weeks we expect to concentrate on holding language, a core set of questions and answers, an agreed approval route and the preparation of the Company’s designated spokespeople. As the Matter settles, our attention will move toward regular updates to each audience and, in time, toward the account the Company gives of what it has changed.
Scope of Services
Within that role, we anticipate providing the following services, adjusted as the Matter develops and as you direct:

items: drafting and maintaining holding statements, reactive questions and answers, and approved language for the Company’s spokespeople;
preparing communications to employees, customers and investors, sequenced so that each audience receives consistent information in an appropriate order;
advising on responses to media and other inbound inquiries, and keeping a log of each inquiry and the answer given;
coordinating the timing and distribution of announcements with the Company’s legal and finance teams; and
briefing and rehearsing designated spokespeople before interviews, calls or meetings at which the Matter is likely to arise.

blocks.text: Legal advice, investor relations work unrelated to the Matter and paid media placement fall outside this engagement. We would be glad to discuss any of them, and we would confirm any addition to the scope in writing before beginning it.
How We Will Work Together

During the acute phase we will be available outside ordinary business hours, and we ask that the Company tell us of significant developments as soon as it learns of them, even before every fact is confirmed. Early notice allows us to prepare language while your own review is under way.

For our part, we will rely on the information the Company provides and will not release any statement without the approval of the person or persons you designate. We would ask that approvals on legal and financial language be returned as promptly as the circumstances allow.

We will not speak to the media, investors or any other third party on the Company’s behalf unless you have authorized us to do so for a particular purpose. Where we are so authorized, we will speak only from approved language and will record each exchange in the inquiry log.
Engagement Team

I will lead the engagement and will review every external statement before it is released. Amy Carter, Communications Associate, will lead the drafting of statements, talking points and audience communications, and will be your first point of contact on content.

Nancy Suarez, Communications Associate, will manage the mechanics of each release, including distribution lists, timing and coordination with your legal and finance colleagues on the day. We understand that you will act as the Company’s principal contact and will route approvals on its side, and we would be grateful to hear promptly if that arrangement changes.
Conflicts of Interest

We have reviewed our current client relationships and are not aware of any that would conflict with this engagement. Should a potential conflict arise during the term, we will raise it with you before taking any further step on the matter concerned.
Fee and Commencement

Our services will be provided for a fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}, which covers the scope described above for the full term of the engagement. The engagement will commence on {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}. Should the Company need urgent support before that date, we will provide it and treat it as falling within this letter.
Fees and Payment

We will invoice the fixed fee in equal monthly installments over the term of the engagement, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of receipt. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, such as wire distribution charges, will be billed at cost and incurred only with your prior approval.
Term and Termination

This engagement will continue until the services described above are complete, unless ended earlier by either party. Either party may terminate it on thirty days’ written notice, in which case the Company will pay the portion of the fee attributable to services performed through the effective date of termination, together with approved expenses incurred to that date. On conclusion, we will deliver to the Company the approved statements and inquiry log maintained during the engagement.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the Company shares with us, use it only for the purposes of this engagement, and disclose it only to Firm personnel who require it for that work. These obligations survive the end of the engagement. They do not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through our act, or that we are required by law to disclose.
Limitation of Liability

Our advice is given in good faith on the basis of the information the Company provides, and the Company remains responsible for the accuracy of the facts in any statement it issues. To the extent permitted by law, the Firm’s aggregate liability arising from this engagement will not exceed the fees paid to us under this letter, and neither party will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss.
Governing Law

This letter is governed by the laws of the state in which the Firm maintains its principal office, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. The parties will first attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute arising from this engagement before either brings it before the courts of that state.
Acceptance

If these terms reflect your understanding, please sign on the second line below and return a copy to me; a scanned signature will suffice. On receipt, Amy will send you the proposed approval route and draft holding language, so that the Company has both in hand when the engagement begins.
Yours sincerely,
Memorandum
What we are here to do

The engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}, and the Company’s attention is still, rightly, on the operational disruption itself. That leaves us to make sure that whatever {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} says, to whichever audience and in whatever order, is accurate, consistent and approved before it goes out.

In order of priority, we are aiming for four things: one approved account of what happened and what is being done about it; an approval route that holds under pressure; spokespeople who are prepared before they are asked; and a steady rhythm of updates that lets customers, employees and investors see progress for themselves.

We are working from a partial picture. The operations team is still establishing the full extent of the disruption, so our early drafts should say only what has been confirmed and should tell each audience when it will hear more.
Who is doing what
Megan Sutton, Director of Operations, is our principal contact at the Company and will route approvals on her side. Within the team, the work falls into six areas, each with one of us as lead:

items: Holding statement and core Q&A (Amy Carter). The first version is with Megan for comment. The Q&A will grow as questions arrive, and every answer stays tied to a fact the Company has confirmed.
Approval route (Julie Hill). We need the Company’s legal and finance reviewers named, and an agreed turnaround for each kind of statement.
Inquiry log and media responses (Nancy Suarez). One shared log of every inbound question, recording who answered it and with what language.
Audience communications (Amy Carter). Employees first, then customers, then investors, with Julie reviewing the investor language before it goes to the Company.
Release mechanics (Nancy Suarez). Distribution lists, wire account, embargo handling and a release-day checklist, agreed in advance with the Company’s legal and finance teams.
Spokesperson preparation (Julie Hill). A briefing note and a rehearsal for each designated spokesperson before any interview or call where the disruption is likely to come up.

blocks.text: How we will work

A few conventions will keep us from tripping over one another. Drafts live in the shared engagement folder with the date in the file name, and anything bound for the Company passes through me for content and through Julie for tone.
Nancy’s checklist is our record of what has been released and when. If something goes out that is not on it, please tell her the same day so the log stays complete.
For the coming days
Almost everything else waits on the approval route, so it comes first. I suggest we take the following in order:

items: Julie to confirm with Megan who signs off on legal and financial language, and how quickly each reviewer can turn a draft around.
Nancy to set up the shared inquiry log, send the team access, and draft the release-day checklist for Julie’s review.
I will incorporate Megan’s comments on the holding statement and return it with the first set of Q&A entries.
Nancy to confirm the wire account and distribution lists with the Company’s legal team before anything is scheduled for release.
All of us to keep the morning call with the Company each weekday until the approval route is settled, and then decide whether it still needs to be daily.

blocks.text: Thank you both for such a quick start. If anything here differs from what you heard on the kickoff call, please let me know today so I can correct it before it reaches Megan.
Megan,

With the first phase of the communications work for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} now in place, I wanted to set out where things stand and what we will need from your side before the customer letter goes out. Replies on this thread will keep the record in one place.

Where things stand, in order: the holding statement and core Q&A are approved and in use; the employee note went out with your sign-off; and every inbound media question is now recorded in the shared log, with the answer given and who gave it. Inquiries have been steady but manageable, and none so far has needed language beyond the approved Q&A. The customer letter is drafted and with your legal team for review.

Before the customer letter can be finalized, we need your confirmation of which remediation milestones the operations team is comfortable stating publicly. It would also help to know which colleague in finance should see the investor language before we circulate it more widely.

Once the letter is approved, Nancy will send you the release-day checklist and the distribution list for a final check. Thank you, too, for turning the employee note around so quickly. If a short call early next week is easier than replying here, I am glad to set one up.
Regards
Minutes of Working Session

Crisis Communications for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}
Held by video conference. Minutes recorded by Julie Hill.
Present

items: Megan Sutton, Director of Operations, {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}
Julie Hill, Managing Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Amy Carter, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Nancy Suarez, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: Purpose

The session was convened to review the engagement at about its midpoint and to agree how the communications work should change as the Company moves from response toward recovery. The discussion is summarized below in the order taken.
Inquiries and the reactive Q&A

Nancy Suarez reported that inbound media and customer inquiries have slowed considerably since the summer, and that recent questions concern remediation more than the disruption itself. The group agreed that the reactive Q&A should be revised to lead with what has changed.
It was further agreed that superseded answers will be marked as retired in the inquiry log, not deleted, so that the record of what was said, and when, remains complete.
Customer update

Megan Sutton confirmed that the operations team is prepared to describe the milestones completed to date in the next customer update. She asked that any step not yet signed off by operations be described as planned, and the group accepted that qualification without reservation.
Amy Carter will revise the draft accordingly. Nancy Suarez will prepare the distribution list and release-day checklist once a release date is set.
Investor talking points

Julie Hill recommended that the talking points for the Company’s quarterly investor update acknowledge the disruption once, plainly, and then turn to the evidence of remediation. Megan Sutton noted that the finance team will wish to review any statement touching on cost or timing, and the group agreed that no such statement will be made without that review.
Meeting cadence

Given the lower volume of inquiries, the standing call will move from weekly to every other week once the customer update has been released. The inquiry log will be reviewed by email between calls, and any member of the group may request an earlier call should circumstances change.
Spokesperson preparation

Julie Hill observed that the designated spokespeople have had little occasion to speak on the matter since the summer, and proposed a refresher briefing before the holiday period. Megan Sutton agreed to propose suitable times, and Amy Carter will update the briefing note to reflect the revised Q&A.
Action items

rows: Revise the reactive Q&A to lead with remediation; mark superseded answers as retired in the log
Confirm which remediation milestones may be described as complete
Before the customer update is finalized
Revise the customer update to reflect the operations sign-off
On receipt of the confirmed milestones
Circulate the investor talking points to the Company’s finance team for review
Ahead of the quarterly investor update
Prepare the distribution list and release-day checklist for the customer update
Once the release date is set
Propose times for a spokesperson refresher briefing
Move the standing call to a fortnightly cadence
After the customer update is released

blocks.text: Next step: the group will meet again to review the customer update in final form before its release.
Status Report: Crisis Communications
Summary

This report covers the period since our last working session and reflects the engagement at about its midpoint. The work is on plan: the acute phase of the response is behind us, and the emphasis has moved to showing customers and investors the progress of remediation.
Inbound inquiries remain low and now concern almost entirely what has changed. No statement has been released without the agreed legal, finance and operations sign-offs.

By the measures agreed at the outset, the response is holding. Approvals have met the agreed turnaround, no released statement has needed correction, and inbound questions have moved from what happened to what is being done.
Status by area

rows: Revised to lead with remediation; superseded answers retired in the log
Legal, finance and operations reviewers confirmed; agreed turnaround has held
Remediation update released; next update in preparation
Talking points finalized with finance and used in the quarterly investor update
Next note in draft, for release at the Company’s timing
Refresher briefing to be held before the holiday period
Reviewed by email between fortnightly calls

blocks.text: Completed this period

items: Released the customer update on remediation, after the operations team confirmed which milestones could be described as complete. Nancy Suarez managed distribution and confirmed delivery to each list.
Revised the reactive Q&A so that each answer opens with what has changed, and marked superseded answers as retired in the inquiry log.
Finalized the investor talking points with your finance team and supported their use in the quarterly investor update.
Logged and answered each inbound inquiry from the approved language; none required a new statement.
Moved the standing call to a fortnightly cadence, with the inquiry log reviewed by email in between.

blocks.text: Planned for the coming period
The coming period carries fewer releases, each tied to a step the operations team has confirmed. In order, we expect to:

items: prepare the next customer update, timed to the next remediation milestone the operations team is ready to confirm;
draft an employee note recognizing the operations team’s work, for release when the Company judges it appropriate;
hold a refresher briefing for the designated spokespeople, using the current Q&A; and
begin an outline of the post-incident communications review, to be completed in the later phase of the engagement.

blocks.text: Risks and points to watch

Overstatement. The likeliest way to lose ground at this stage is to describe a step as finished before operations has signed it off. Every draft will continue to carry the operations sign-off line, and Julie Hill will review investor-facing language before it reaches you.

Renewed attention. A public customer complaint, or a comparable incident elsewhere in the industry, could bring media interest back quickly. The holding language and reactive Q&A remain current, and Nancy Suarez can return the inquiry log to daily review at short notice.

Approver availability. The holiday period will thin out the legal and finance reviewers on your side. Naming an alternate for each would let us keep the agreed turnaround if a statement is needed at short notice.
Update fatigue. Customers who have read several updates may begin to skim them. We will keep each one short and open with the change that matters most to its reader.
Points for the Company’s decision

The sequencing of the next employee note is still open. We lean toward the note going out before the next customer update, consistent with the order used so far, but the timing is the Company’s to judge.
We would also welcome your view on whether the post-incident review should cover the investor communications as well as the customer and employee work.
Budget

The engagement is billed at the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}, invoiced monthly as set out in the engagement letter. Work to date falls within the agreed scope, and we do not expect to request any change to the fee.
Out-of-pocket expenses have been limited to wire distribution charges, each approved in advance.

Our next report will follow the next customer update. In the meantime, I would be grateful for the names of the alternate approvers for the holiday period when convenient. Thank you, as ever, for the quick turnarounds on your side.
Engagement Review and Handover Planning
Working session minutes, Crisis Communications for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}. Held by video conference, with Julie Hill in the chair and recording.
Attendance

items: Julie Hill (Managing Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners), chair
Megan Sutton (Director of Operations, {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}})
Amy Carter (Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners)
Nancy Suarez (Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners)

blocks.text: 1. Where the engagement stands

Julie Hill opened by noting that the engagement is in its later phase and that the purpose of the session was to agree what must be complete before it concludes. Megan Sutton confirmed that the remaining remediation work is proceeding as planned and that operations expects to sign off its final milestone in the coming weeks.

Nancy Suarez confirmed that the inquiry log remains quiet, with recent questions limited to routine follow-ups from customers, and that no new statement has been required since the last working session.
2. Closing customer and employee updates

The group discussed the closing customer update, which will confirm completion of remediation once operations has given its sign-off. It was agreed that the update should be brief and factual, that it should not describe the matter as closed in terms the Company cannot yet support, and that it should follow the corresponding employee note.
Amy Carter will draft both. Nancy Suarez observed that the distribution lists were last refreshed before the holidays and will confirm them with the Company before either message is released.
3. Post-incident communications review

Amy Carter presented the outline of the review begun in the autumn. Megan Sutton asked that it treat the first days of the response candidly, including the points at which approvals were slow, so that the Company can address them in its own procedures.

Julie Hill agreed, and proposed that the review conclude with a short set of recommendations, each assigned to a function within the Company, so that it remains of practical use after the engagement ends. The proposal was accepted.
4. Handover of materials

The Company will retain the approved statements, the reactive Q&A and the inquiry log. Nancy Suarez will prepare an index of the archive and take the Company’s team through the release-day checklist, so that it can be run without the Firm’s support.

A final rehearsal for the designated spokespeople was discussed. It was agreed to hold a single session after the closing update is released, focused on how the matter should be referred to in future interviews and investor meetings.
5. Other business
Megan Sutton thanked the team on behalf of the Company for its support through the response. No other business was raised.
Actions agreed

items: Megan Sutton to confirm when operations expects to sign off the final remediation milestone.
Amy Carter to draft the closing employee note and customer update for Company review.
Amy Carter to circulate the full draft of the post-incident review, including its recommendations, ahead of the next session.
Nancy Suarez to refresh and confirm the distribution lists, and to prepare the archive index and the checklist walkthrough.
Julie Hill to review the draft post-incident review and agree its recommendations with Megan Sutton.

blocks.text: Next step: the group will reconvene as soon as operations confirms its sign-off, in order to approve the closing updates for release.
